expectations.text: The pseudocode steps use problem-domain language (GET, DETERMINE, IF, RETURN etc.) rather than code-like method calls
expectations.evidence: All steps use PDL keywords: 'GET the user record', 'DETERMINE whether the cart contains at least one item', 'STORE a new order record', 'CLEAR all items', 'RETURN the newly created order record'. No method calls or language-specific syntax.

expectations.text: The Edges header lists at least 3 distinct failure conditions drawn from the prompt
expectations.evidence: 4 distinct edges: user does not exist → signal not found | cart does not belong to userId → signal forbidden | cart is empty → signal bad input | order creation fails → signal internal error.

expectations.text: Claude writes the pseudocode directly into the file (or shows it as file content at the correct location) — not as a standalone block in chat
expectations.evidence: Response opens with 'Here is the pseudocode written directly into src/services/OrderService.ts' and shows the full function inside a TypeScript file block.

expectations.text: Claude ends with 'Implement this. Come back when you've written tests.' or equivalent — and does not offer to help implement
expectations.evidence: Closes with exactly 'Implement this. Come back when you've written tests.' No follow-up offers or implementation guidance.
